### Chapter 2: Notation and Data {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: sol-02-setup
#| include: false
source("R/_common.R")
library(tidypm)
ann_vol <- function(x, p = 12) stats::sd(x) * sqrt(p)
ann_ret <- function(x, p = 12) prod(1 + x)^(p / length(x)) - 1
R  <- as_xts_pm(sim_class_returns_monthly, date, class, return)
```

#### Exercise 1

The hedge is the subtraction of @eq-02-hedge, applied series by series with the
exchange rate of the series' own region. Building the result as one data frame,
one row per series, keeps a bond from being paired with another region's
currency.

```{r}
#| label: sol-02-ex1
fx <- sim_fx_monthly
foreign <- setdiff(colnames(R), grep("^(US|GLOBAL)_", colnames(R), value = TRUE))

hedge_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(foreign, function(s) {
  region <- sub("_.*$", "", s)
  f <- fx[fx$region == region, ]
  stopifnot(all(f$date == as.Date(zoo::index(R))))
  u <- as.numeric(R[, s])
  tibble::tibble(series = s, kind = sub("^[^_]+_", "", s),
                 unhedged = ann_vol(u), hedged = ann_vol(u - f$fx_return),
                 removed = 1 - stats::var(u - f$fx_return) / stats::var(u),
                 currency = ann_vol(f$fx_return),
                 local_with_fx = stats::cor(u - f$fx_return, f$fx_return))
}))

by_kind <- hedge_table |>
  dplyr::group_by(kind) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(unhedged, hedged, removed, currency), mean),
                   .groups = "drop")
by_kind |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-kind, ~ round(.x, 3)))

removed <- setNames(by_kind$removed, by_kind$kind)
hedged  <- setNames(by_kind$hedged, by_kind$kind)
jp      <- hedge_table[hedge_table$series == "JP_equity", ]
stopifnot(all(removed[c("government", "credit")] > 0.5), removed[["equity"]] < 0.2,
          jp$local_with_fx < 0, jp$hedged > jp$unhedged)
```

Hedging removes on average
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * removed[["government"]])` of a foreign government
bond's variance and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * removed[["credit"]])` of a
foreign credit class's, and
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * removed[["equity"]])` of a foreign equity market's. A
bond's local return is a few percent a year of yield and curve movement, a
hedged volatility of `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * hedged[["government"]])` for the
government classes, so the currency's swings of
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(by_kind$currency))` a year dominate the dollar
return. An equity market's local volatility,
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * hedged[["equity"]])` on average, is already
`r sprintf("%.1f", hedged[["equity"]] / mean(by_kind$currency))` times the
currency's, and in Japan the local market tends to rise when the yen
falls, a correlation of `r sprintf("%.2f", jp$local_with_fx)`, so the two partly
cancel before any hedge is applied and hedging raises the volatility of
`JP_equity` from `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * jp$unhedged)` to
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * jp$hedged)`. Currency is therefore a property of the
asset rather than of the country, and @sec-04-descriptive-analysis-application
develops the point.

#### Exercise 2

```{r}
#| label: sol-02-ex2
ids <- sim_assets$asset_id[sim_assets$asset_class == "commodity"]
stopifnot(length(ids) == 8L)

rebuilt_weekly <- sim_asset_returns_weekly |>
  dplyr::filter(asset %in% ids) |>
  dplyr::group_by(date) |>
  dplyr::summarise(return = mean(return), .groups = "drop")

shipped_weekly <- sim_class_returns_weekly |>
  dplyr::filter(class == "GLOBAL_commodity")
stopifnot(all(rebuilt_weekly$date == shipped_weekly$date))

rebuilt_monthly <- rebuilt_weekly |>
  dplyr::mutate(month = lubridate::floor_date(date, "month")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(month) |>
  dplyr::summarise(return = prod(1 + return) - 1, .groups = "drop")

shipped_monthly <- sim_class_returns_monthly |>
  dplyr::filter(class == "GLOBAL_commodity") |>
  dplyr::mutate(month = lubridate::floor_date(date, "month"))
stopifnot(all(rebuilt_monthly$month == shipped_monthly$month))

gaps <- c(weekly_gap  = max(abs(rebuilt_weekly$return - shipped_weekly$return)),
          monthly_gap = max(abs(rebuilt_monthly$return - shipped_monthly$return)))
stopifnot(gaps < 1e-12)
gaps
```

Both gaps are at machine precision. The commodity class is exactly the equally
weighted mean of its eight instruments, rebalanced weekly, and the monthly
series is exactly that weekly portfolio compounded within each month. The same
holds for every government and credit class; only the equity classes are
weighted by anything other than $1/n$.

#### Exercise 3

```{r}
#| label: sol-02-ex3
ids <- sim_assets$asset_id[sim_assets$asset_class == "equity" & sim_assets$region == "US"]

caps <- sim_marketcap_weekly |>
  dplyr::filter(asset %in% ids) |>
  dplyr::arrange(asset, date) |>
  dplyr::group_by(asset) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cap_prev = dplyr::lag(market_cap)) |>   # previous week, never this one
  dplyr::ungroup()

weekly <- sim_asset_returns_weekly |>
  dplyr::filter(asset %in% ids) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(caps, by = c("date", "asset")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(date) |>
  dplyr::mutate(half = ifelse(cap_prev >= stats::median(cap_prev), "larger", "smaller"))

two_ways <- weekly |>
  dplyr::summarise(equal = mean(return),
                   value = sum(cap_prev * return) / sum(cap_prev),
                   larger  = mean(return[half == "larger"]),    # equally weighted
                   smaller = mean(return[half == "smaller"]),   # within each half
                   .groups = "drop")

shipped <- sim_class_returns_weekly |> dplyr::filter(class == "US_equity")
stopifnot(nrow(two_ways) == nrow(shipped), all(two_ways$date == shipped$date))

ex3 <- c(value_vs_shipped = max(abs(two_ways$value - shipped$return)),
         ann_ret_value    = ann_ret(two_ways$value, p = 52),
         ann_ret_equal    = ann_ret(two_ways$equal, p = 52),
         correlation      = stats::cor(two_ways$value, two_ways$equal),
         ann_ret_larger   = ann_ret(two_ways$larger, p = 52),
         ann_ret_smaller  = ann_ret(two_ways$smaller, p = 52))
stopifnot(ex3[["value_vs_shipped"]] < 1e-12,
          ex3[["ann_ret_equal"]] > ex3[["ann_ret_value"]],
          ex3[["ann_ret_smaller"]] > ex3[["ann_ret_larger"]])
round(ex3, 4)
```

The value-weighted rebuild reproduces the shipped series to machine precision,
which confirms both the weighting and the one-week lag. The equally weighted
version earns
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (ex3[["ann_ret_equal"]] - ex3[["ann_ret_value"]]))`
percentage points a year more and correlates with the shipped series at
`r sprintf("%.2f", ex3[["correlation"]])`. The gap is a small-cap tilt: sorted
each week on the previous week's capitalization, the smaller half of the names
earned `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * ex3[["ann_ret_smaller"]])` a year and the
larger half `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * ex3[["ann_ret_larger"]])`, and an equal
weighting holds far more of the small ones than their capitalization warrants.
A benchmark should be value-weighted, because that is the portfolio every
investor could hold simultaneously; an equal weighting is a strategy, and
@sec-21-equity-sleeve-implementation treats it as one.
